description:
Two storey side to rear extension to create semi detached dwelling
(1 x 2 bed); alterations to roof; rear dormer; two rooflights in front
roofslope; external alterations; parking; landscaping; separate
amenity space; bin and cycle stores (demolition of attached garage
and side extension)
decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-top: 0cm; margin-right: 0cm; margin-bottom: 0cm; text-align: justify; text-indent: -36pt; line-height: normal;"><span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;</span>The
proposed development, by reason of its design, scale and increase in intensity
of use as a separate, independent dwellinghouse, would unbalance the proportions
of the existing dwelling and result in an end of terrace dwelllinghouse that
would be out of keeping with the prevailing pattern of development. The
proposed development would be at odds with the established character of the site
and wider streetscene from a visual and use perspective. &nbsp;The proposal is therefore found to be contrary
to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy GR1 and Policy GR10 of the
Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041). &nbsp;<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align: justify; text-indent: -36pt;"><span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; </span>By reason of the absence of a submitted independent,
compliant Fire Safety Strategy, the proposed development fails to demonstrate
that fire safety matters have been adequately incorporated into the planning
and design stage for the proposed
dwellinghouse, contrary to the provisions of Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021)
and Policy GR3B.C of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align: justify; text-indent: -36pt;"><span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;</span>The cumulative impacts of the two proposed car
parking spaces, alongside the area marked for waste collection to serve the two
properties and transfer of bins on collection day to the frontage cannot be
satisfactorily provided within the front forecourt of the site to meet the
Council's requirements. This would result in visual clutter which would be
detrimental to the character and appearance of the area, impede upon pedestrian
access to No. 27 and the property entrance of the newly proposed dwelling No. 27A
and wider highway safety and adversely impact&nbsp; highway safety. The
proposal is therefore contrary to National Planning Policy Framework (2024),
Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies GR1, M1 and CE1(B) of the
Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).<o:p></o:p></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-align: justify;">A Preliminary Roost Appraisal (PRA) is absent from the
planning application submission material, which is required prior to
determination. In the absence of such ecological information, the Local
Planning Authority is unable to determine whether roosting bats likely occupy
any crevices or voids present on the building. Further emergence surveys may be
required following the initial PRA. This is to ensure that the proposed works
would not affect roosting bats in accordance with Section 41 of the Natural
Environmental and Rural Communities Act 2006 (NERC), The Conservation of
Habitats and Species Regulations (2019), Schedules 1, 5 and 8 of the Wildlife
and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended), the ODPM Circular 06/2005: Biodiversity
and Geological Conservation – Statutory Obligations and their impact within the
Planning System, and would therefore be contrary to Paragraph 187 of the
National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021)
and Strategic Policy 07 and Policy GI 3 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).<o:p></o:p></p>
